module purpose: This block stores bus-written enable, lock, strict, and timeout control state, counts prescaled ticks while enabled, accepts a matching service write to clear the count, asserts rstn_o low on timeout or strict access faults, drives clkgen_en_o from the enable bit, and records a reset-cause code for readback.

use-case flows.value: control-register update of enable, lock, strict, and timeout when a write targets the control address and the block is not locked
stored lock state blocks later control-register writes and turns a blocked write into reset_force
the enable state turns on clkgen_en_o and allows counting to start on prescaler ticks
prescaled count progression and timeout comparison while enabled
a matching service-register write produces reset_wdt and clears the counter
timeout or strict access fault latches internal reset requests and drives rstn_o low
reset-cause code captured from external reset, debug reset, timeout reset, or access reset
stored enable, lock, reset cause, strict, and timeout values returned on bus reads
system and external resets clear stored control, counter, reset-request, and cause state

conceptual assets.concept: Watchdog enable state — whether counting and reset generation are active
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure and start flows store ctrl.enable from the control write at line 94, use it to start counting at line 130, force the counter idle/reset path at line 131 when disabled, drive clkgen_en_o at line 140, and qualify both reset-request generators at lines 155-156. Corrupting this stored bit makes the implemented start, counting, and reset behavior incorrect; availability is also established because the bit is retained until overwritten or rstn_sys_i clears it at line 75.

conceptual assets.concept: Configuration lock state — whether the control register can still be rewritten
conceptual assets.reasoning: The lock flow stores ctrl.lock at line 95, tests it before permitting later control writes at line 93, and routes a blocked write to reset_force at line 99. Corrupting this state breaks the implemented protection relation between the lock setting and later writes; availability is also established because the stored bit persists until rstn_sys_i clears it at line 76. Its readback at line 110 is on the bus transport port, so the stored field is the eligible structural reference here.

conceptual assets.concept: Strict access-reset mode — whether a forbidden access escalates to hardware reset
conceptual assets.reasoning: The strict setting is stored at line 96 and then consumed in `hw_rst_access <= ctrl.enable and ctrl.strict and reset_force` at line 156. Corrupting ctrl.strict changes whether the implemented access-fault path can assert a reset request; availability is also established because the setting is retained until rstn_sys_i clears it at line 77. Its readback at line 112 is on the excluded bus transport port.

conceptual assets.concept: Timeout threshold configuration — the stored count value that defines expiration
conceptual assets.reasoning: The timeout field is stored from the control write at line 97, compared against the running count at line 144, and thereby influences timeout reset generation at line 155. Corrupting this stored value changes the implemented expiration point of the timer; availability is also established because the threshold is retained until rstn_sys_i clears it at line 78. Its readback at line 113 is on the excluded bus transport port.

conceptual assets.concept: Watchdog progress state — whether timing has started and the current count value
conceptual assets.reasoning: The operate flow stores cnt_started at line 130 and cnt at lines 132-134. Those stored states are the basis of the timeout test at line 144, so corrupting either changes when timeout is or is not recognized. Availability is also established because, with ctrl.enable set and no service reset, cnt_started advances from prsc_tick at line 130 and cnt increments at line 134; rstn_sys_i clears them at lines 126-127.

conceptual assets.concept: Watchdog service-accept decision — one-cycle authorization to clear the count
conceptual assets.reasoning: The reset flow only sets reset_wdt when a write targets the service address and the written 32-bit value matches the required constant at lines 101-103; line 131 then uses `reset_wdt = '1'` to clear cnt at line 132. Corrupting this decision would accept an incorrect service write or reject a correct one, breaking the implemented counter-clear rule; availability is also established because the pulse is produced for the matching write and otherwise cleared at lines 79 and 87.

conceptual assets.concept: Timeout reset request — the latched timeout-driven reset decision sent on rstn_o
conceptual assets.reasoning: The operate/reset flow computes timeout at line 144 and then latches `hw_rst_timeout <= ctrl.enable and cnt_timeout and prsc_tick` at line 155; rstn_o is driven low from that request or hw_rst_access at line 161, and line 174 records the timeout cause. Corrupting this decision changes whether the implemented timeout event resets the system; availability is also established because, when the enabled counter reaches the stored threshold and a prescaler tick occurs, the request is produced and delivered on rstn_o.

conceptual assets.concept: Strict-access reset request — the latched reset decision after a forbidden access
conceptual assets.reasoning: Forbidden writes set reset_force at lines 99 or 105, and line 156 latches `hw_rst_access <= ctrl.enable and ctrl.strict and reset_force`; rstn_o is then driven low at line 161 and line 176 records the access-reset cause. Corrupting this decision changes whether the implemented strict access-fault path resets the system; availability is also established because, when those conditions hold, the request is produced and delivered on rstn_o.

conceptual assets.concept: Recorded reset-cause code — stored classification of the last reset source
conceptual assets.reasoning: The report flow stores 00 on rstn_ext_i low at line 169, 01 on rstn_dbg_i low at line 172, 10 on hw_rst_timeout at line 174, and 11 on hw_rst_access at line 176, and line 111 returns that code on bus reads. Corrupting reset_cause misreports which implemented event last caused reset; availability is also established because the code is retained until external reset or a later qualifying event overwrites it.
